title: 亚市早盘美股期货上涨，市场聚焦债券收益率
content:
在亚洲早盘交易中，美国股指期货上涨，在华尔街尾盘大幅波动抹平了由低于预期的通胀数据引发的涨幅后，新季度伊始的市场情绪趋于稳定。
标普500指数期货上涨0.2%。此前在周三交易最后几个小时，该指数抹平了涨幅，最终收跌0.2%。 美光 科技给出了乐观的业绩预期，但警告称不断上升的薪酬成本将拖累利润率，受此影响，亚洲股市预计开盘走势分化。
在全球政府债券经历了自2024年以来表现最差的一个季度后，债券收益率继续成为市场焦点。油价突破100美元，加剧了世界经济面临顽固通胀的威胁。美国30年期国债收益率再次攀升，刷新了2002年以来的最高水平。货币市场预计美联储10月份加息的概率不到40%。
在亚洲早盘交易中，美国原油价格小幅回落至每桶90.10美元，维持了前一交易日的涨幅。与此同时，美元结束了自3月份以来表现最好的一个月。

title: “大空头”伯里：若股市崩溃阻止OpenAI和Anthropic上市，将是人类幸事
content:
电影《大空头》原型人物迈克尔·伯里（Michael Burry）表示，如果市场崩盘导致美国两家最大的人工智能公司无法上市，这对人类将是有益的。
这位知名投资者周二在社交平台X上发帖称：“为了人类的利益，市场应当大幅暴跌，从而阻止OpenAI和Anthropic的IPO。”
在后续的回复中，伯里针对其原帖提供了更多细节。他表示，这些公司将“吸纳”并随后毁灭“数万亿美元的资本”，并补充道，这还仅仅是它们造成的“最小的破坏”。
伯里还回复了一位用户的调侃——该用户打趣说要“搞垮市场，好让‘天网’（Skynet）无法IPO”（“天网”是电影《终结者》中那个具有毁灭性的人工智能系统）。
无论伯里（Burry）预想的是何种更广泛的后果，这两家公司所涉及的经济利益已然巨大。
OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥特曼本月早些时候表示，鉴于对人工智能安全性的担忧，在 2026 年进行首次公开募股（IPO）将是“不明智的”。与此同时，一份招股说明书显示，Anthropic 可能会在11月美国中期选举后进行 IPO。
这两家公司都需要投入巨额资金来开发先进模型并构建支撑这些模型的计算基础设施。通过上市，它们能够接触到更广泛的投资者群体，从而获得更充裕的资金。
伯里本周在 Substack 上发文称，他“比以往任何时候都更有信心”，认为自己关于人工智能（AI）的看空观点将在未来一年内应验，这将使他此前预期的2028年AI泡沫破裂这一基准时间点提前到来。
这位投资者表示，出于坚定的判断，他再次加大了针对一系列标的（包括英伟达、Palantir、 美光 、 甲骨文 以及 纳斯达克 100指数）的做空押注。
伯里认为，这种由债务驱动的芯片和数据中心支出是不可持续的，且极易受到利率上升的冲击。他写道，一旦支出放缓，“一切都会崩塌”。
然而，尽管存在种种担忧，人工智能（AI）相关股票今年仍一路高歌猛进，屡创历史新高。

title: 微软科学总裁彼得·李将离职
content: 周三， 微软 资深高管彼得·李（Peter Lee）宣布将离开公司。多年来，他一直领导着微软的内部研究部门。李是今年宣布离职的微软多名高级主管之一。今年以来，Office和Windows业务负责人拉杰什·贾（Rajesh Jha）、Xbox首席执行官菲尔·斯宾塞（Phil Spencer）、首席通信官弗兰克·肖（Frank Shaw）以及安全主管查理·贝尔（Charlie Bell）均已宣布离职计划。彼得·李于2010年加入微软，协助领导一个拥有约1500名科学家的研究部门。该部门致力于研究与微软业务相关的多个领域，包括人工智能、量子计算、搜索、机器人技术和密码学等。这些研究成果催生了多款微软新产品，其中包括微软去年推出的量子计算芯片，公司表示该芯片有望塑造计算技术的未来。

title: US death row inmate survives execution attempt after two lethal injections
content:
Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike has been taken to hospital after an attempt to execute her by two lethal injections failed, her lawyer says.

Her legal team filed an emergency motion to halt the convicted murderer's execution as it was happening, saying: "Ms Pike has lost consciousness and still has a heartbeat and is audibly snoring."

One of her attorneys told the BBC that Pike, 50, was now "being provided life-saving measures" in hospital after two syringes of pentobarbital had been administered.

Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Her execution was the subject of a last-minute legal battle.

This culminated in the US Supreme Court allowing the lethal injections to go ahead.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens.

Slemmer's mother May Martinez was among those who wanted the execution to take place. Speaking to NBC News after Wednesday evening's events, she said: "It was a mess."

The attempted execution took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 20:00 local time (01:00 GMT on Thursday).

Pike was given two doses of the chemical pentobarbital, and the curtain in the witness room was closed twice, the AP news agency reported.

Media were at some point asked to leave, the news agency said.

AP added that Tennessee's execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes in case the person being put to death does not die after the first set. But it does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set.

Why there was a surge of US executions in 2025

LISTEN: Could the US death penalty ever die out?

In a statement reported by US media, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee said he had ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred". He said the year's last remaining execution would not go ahead as planned.

The attempted execution of Pike was not the first in the state in 2026 that did not unfold as planned. The execution of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed in May after staff were unable to find a vein to administer a lethal drug.

The Tennessee Department of Correction has said it stands by all the actions it took during the attempted execution of Pike.

"The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the State's lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General's Office," department spokesperson Dorinda Carter told the Tennessean newspaper.

"The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility," she said.

Pike's legal team said in a statement to the Tennessean newspaper: "Tonight the State of Tennessee once again failed to carry out a lawful execution.

"We take no pleasure in being right, but the concerns raised by Ms Pike proved to be true: difficult vein access, blown veins, degraded pentobarbital, no emergency medical care available when things inevitably go wrong, all under a protocol that remains veiled in secrecy."

Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion to stay her execution and provide medical care after the lethal injection was apparently botched.

District Judge Clifton L Corker issued a ruling noting that "medical personnel have begun to administer medical care as requested in the motion".

Dr Joel Zivot, a professor at the Emory University School of Medicine who told the BBC he had been retained by Pike's legal team as a medical expert, said she likely never achieved a sufficient blood level of pentobarbital to cause apnoea and cardiovascular failure during the attempted execution.

"It's very possible that as a consequence of the delay of the beginning of resuscitation she will have a brain injury," Zivot said in an email.

The attempted capital punishment went ahead after multiple last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers failed.

The US Supreme Court had thwarted two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.

Late on Wednesday, America's highest court overturned a reprieve granted by a lower court earlier in the day. The lower court had granted a pause, saying it needed more time to consider the arguments in Pike's case.

The Supreme Court had previously dismissed an appeal by Pike's lawyers, who had argued the jury did not get the chance to weigh mitigating evidence of Pike's documented history of childhood sexual abuse, before they sentenced her to death in 1996.

The defence said that for years, the state of Tennessee had argued in court that she lied about being sexually abused as a child.

But at a recent hearing about her execution method, the state said it did not dispute that she had suffered sexual abuse and rape.

Tennessee's governor denied a clemency request this week from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.

In her clemency petition, Pike said that she intended to beat Slemmer, not kill her, but that she was unable to "put the brakes on".

"I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid," she said in a statement. "It took me numerous years to even realise the gravity of what I'd done. Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone's child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime."

The murder in 1995 created a media frenzy in Knoxville, Tennessee, after Colleen was found with an inverted pentagram - a symbol that is associated with satanic groups - carved into her chest. Pike has denied carving the symbol herself.

Before the killing, Pike had accused Colleen of insulting her and trying to steal her then-boyfriend.

Two other residents at the camp later testified that Pike had bragged about the murder before and after, and showed them a piece of Colleen's skull.

Pike's boyfriend and co-defendant Shipp was 17 at the time so spared the death penalty under state law. He remains in prison.

Martinez, Slemmer's mother, said at the weekend that she had waited decades to see Pike's sentence carried out.

She told AP that a group helped raise funds for her and her husband to travel from Florida to Tennessee to witness the execution.

"Not a day goes by, or a minute goes by that I do not think about Colleen. Holidays are the worst," Martinez said.

Since 1976, when the Supreme Court resumed the death penalty, only 18 women have been executed in the US, compared to 1,663 men. That is about 1% of all US executions.

title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest
content:
The winning entry of a prestigious scientific photography competition is being re-evaluated following criticism from other scientists that it was made with AI.

Nikon's annual Small World In Motion contest accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes, and has run annually for the last 15 years.

The winner was a short video submitted by Dr Ning Xu, a researcher at Tsinghua University in China, which claims to be footage of tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving inside the airways of a child with a rare disease.

Xu did not respond to the BBC's request for comment, but has posted online denying he broke the competition rules.

In a response to a post by Nikon on LinkedIn, external, he did not dispute using AI within the image processing but said he remained within the rules of the contest.

"AI was not used to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion," he said.

Xu's video is artificially brightly coloured - common in microscopy and permitted in the contest - which is usually done manually using stains and dyes on the sample itself.

He accepted AI was used "to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images".

But the challenges made by other scientists include claims that the video contains shapes and movements which did not fit with normal cell structures or behaviours, and that the cilia seemed to be too big.

Commenting on Nikon's social media post, Edward Phelps, associate professor at Florida University, observed some of the structures "pop in and out of existence" and the cilia "appear from nowhere".

Meanwhile PhD student Ian Donovan from UT Southwestern Medical Centre said the source image appeared to contain a distinctive watermark indicating it had been AI generated.

Additionally, two former competition judges said they also had concerns about whether the image was real.

'Respectfully complying'

Nikon said Xu was "respectfully complying" with its investigation and had provided it with additional technical documents.

Dr Patrick Hickey, who came fifth in the 2026 Small World contest, said the recognition the award represents means more than the $3,000 (£2,250) prize itself.

"If you spend a lot of your time in a dark room looking down a microscope, it's really nice to be able to show people and to show the public," he said.

"There's an interesting fusion between science and art, and a lot of the images that scientists are making have some very abstract and artistic qualities to them."

Hickey said it would be unfair on other entrants if it turned out the winning video was unfairly altered by AI.

"There's a specific set of rules in the contest, and one of them was quite clearly that you couldn't use generative AI to produce things, and the other was obviously that it has to be taken under a microscope," he said.

So far, Nikon is standing by its procedures but it said there would be an update soon.

"At this time, we don't see that any rules were violated," it said in a statement.

title: Rosenberg: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
content:
When Vladimir Putin arrived to address Russia's parliament on Wednesday, a warm welcome was guaranteed.

"The Special Election Operation", as one Russian newspaper dubbed last month's legislative vote, has produced a State Duma even more pro-Putin than anything before it.

The ruling party, United Russia, now has more MPs than ever.

It allows the Kremlin to claim it has been handed a huge mandate from the Russian people.

But for what? How will Putin use it?

Are there any signs he is prepared to halt what he calls the special military operation? Or should we brace for further escalation in Ukraine and in tensions with Europe?

On Thursday I'll be watching to see whether Russia's leader sheds light on his plans during an appearance at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow. Traditionally the president's speech at this annual foreign policy forum provides insight into Putin's world view.

Right now, everything points to Putin continuing Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine: despite his country's huge battlefield losses to date and the damage being done to Russia's economy.

Putin's speeches and statements suggest he remains confident that Russia can secure a military victory.

Judging by what is being reported in Russian media, Moscow is encouraged by the shortage of air defence missiles in Ukraine, as well as the expectation that Russian strikes this winter will increase pressure on Ukrainians. Kyiv has spoken of its difficulty in shooting down Russia's ballistic missiles and new jet-powered drones, which have been targeting Ukraine every day.

And further afield?

The Kremlin has made no secret of the fact it wants European states to slash their military and financial backing for Ukraine: the kind of support Moscow says is prolonging the war - or, rather, getting in the way of a Russian victory.

To achieve this, Western officials believe Russia has been sending not so subtle signals.

They accuse Moscow of waging an escalating hybrid war on European countries through cyber-attacks, acts of sabotage, and Russian drones violating European airspace. In Germany, a drone carrying an explosive device was found close to Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig airport.

A covert campaign in the "grey zone", that space between peace and war.

This week I asked Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, does he admit that his country is waging a hybrid war against European countries?

"Do you mean when we destroy drones and missiles that Britain and continental Europe are supplying Ukraine with, and which are used to attack us?" Lavrov replied.

"If you admit your weapons are being used to strike us and we destroy them, call it whatever you want. But I have no doubt this is a war Europe is waging against us. We've been saying so for a long time."

That, indeed, has been the official Russian stance for some time: that what is happening in Ukraine amounts to a European war on Russia. It is a narrative that skips over the fact that in 2022 it was the Kremlin that launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and that Russia continues to wage war there.

How far would Russia go to sever European support for Kyiv?

Is Moscow, for example, actively preparing to initiate military conflict in Europe with a Nato member state? That seems unlikely. After more than four-and-a-half years of war Russia's army has not yet managed to occupy the whole of Ukraine's eastern Donbas region, right next door to Russia.

Fighting Europe may not be the plan, but freaking it out, to reduce support for Kyiv, could well be the intention.

Listen to the messaging.

"If they continue this war, a European war with American help, against Russia, on Ukrainian territory, sooner or later we'll feel the need to escalate," warns prominent foreign policy strategist Sergei Karaganov, honorary chairman of Russia's Council for Foreign and Defence Policy.

"According to my scenarios, the first series of blows will be conventional," he told me. "But if Europe does not surrender, unfortunately, we will have to go nuclear. There will be little left of some European countries."

But if Russia went nuclear there would be a response from Europe, and nothing would be left of Russia, I suggest.

"No, there will be no response from Europe," said Karaganov. "What, Britain will attack Russia with nuclear weapons? I hope you're not that crazy. I'm sure the Americans are not that crazy."

I asked him if he agreed the last four-and-a-half years had been disastrous for Russia, in terms of casualties and the worsening security and economic situation.

"We've lost a lot of people, yes," he admitted, "and I criticise my government for not being rough enough. But now we are getting rough enough in Ukraine. We're doing away with Ukraine as a viable state."

If "doing away with Ukraine as a viable state" is Moscow's goal, it is hard to imagine the war ending soon.

Meanwhile, Russia continues to rail against what it sees as the double standards of the West. In his recent address at the UN General Assembly, Sergei Lavrov accused the West of resorting to "brute force" around the world.

"What they did in Venezuela, was that soft power or brute force?" Russia's foreign minister asked me this week. He was referring to America's military operation in Caracas to capture Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro back in January.

"The fact that [the US] bombed and destroyed Iran's leadership, along with their families, including children, is that not brute force?"

But was Russia not resorting to brute force every day in Ukraine, I replied.

"If you mean the destruction of infrastructure used by a Nazi regime backed by the West to wage war on the Russian Federation, then we are resorting to brute force to eliminate this direct threat to us."

Not only is this another element of Russia's official narrative: painting Ukraine as a neo-Nazi state, creating a false pretext to justify Russia's actions.

With the admission of Russia's use of "brute force" in Ukraine, it is also further evidence that Moscow is in no mood to stop fighting.

title: 派拉蒙任命克雷兹为联合首席执行官 华纳兄弟并购交易临近完成
content: 派拉蒙天舞公司（Paramount Skydance Corp．）的大卫·埃里森（David Ellison）表示，在完成对探索 华纳 兄弟公司（Warner Bros． Discovery Inc．）的1100亿美元待决收购后，前美泰公司（Mattel Inc．）首席执行官伊农·克雷兹（Ynon Kreiz）将出任合并后公司的联席首席执行官。根据派拉蒙周三发布的一份声明，埃里森将继续担任该公司的董事长。公司高管将同时向两人汇报工作。埃里森表示：“伊农是一位具备强大领导力和运营实力的合作伙伴，这正是此次整合所需要的。”此次任命只是派拉蒙预期中多项领导层变动之一。随着埃里森组建一支融合了华纳兄弟顶尖人才与克雷兹等资深高管的团队，他将负责管理这场复杂的合并交易。该交易将把两大电影制片厂、流媒体平台、电视网络资产以及新闻媒体整合在同一所有权之下。加州一名联邦法官签署了一项协议，解决了 12 位反对合并的州检察长提起的诉讼，从而为合并完成扫清了障碍。

title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest
content:
When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.

"It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits. "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning."

He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful. "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe. How long do you have to pick it?" he says. "That's where these models are really helpful."

Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example. The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity. Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.

But planning a harvest is tricky. New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging. It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly. Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.

Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines. The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by. AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.

"Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter. He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.

But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter. "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains. "It's going to be bespoke to your farm."

Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter. For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.

"If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.

His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes. "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.

Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask? Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas. "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't."

The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.

This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK. This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.

The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts. The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate). We guarantee less than 20% error…"

Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast. AI tech for forecasting fruit ripeness is not yet "a finished solution" says operations director Neill Finlayson: "This journey is still ongoing and, whilst significant progress has been made, the industry remains some way from achieving a fully integrated forecasting ecosystem."

Driscoll's, a California headquartered fruit seller with a big operation in the UK, also confirmed to BBC News that some of its independent fruit growers in the UK have used FruitCast's technology.

Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail. Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop. These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.

Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements. But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.

She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector, external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops. Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey. "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.

Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.

But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile. "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University. "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works."

Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries, external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.

The simplest systems need not be expensive. Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery, external from $100 (£74) drones.

In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions. However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.

Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US. He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".

But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence. "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.

title: Vape tax comes into effect - but prices won't rise yet
content:
The price of vapes is set to rise as a new tax comes into effect, with the aim of making vaping less attractive to children and young people.

The Vaping Product Duty will be imposed at a rate of £2.20 per 10ml of e-liquid. However, many customers will not see a jump in prices immediately, as sellers have six months to sell old stock at the pre-duty price.

The government wants to reduce the appeal of vapes by making them more expensive, as more evidence of its adverse effect on health comes out, particularly on children and young people.

The vaping industry has lobbied against the new tax, saying that affordable vapes help people to quit smoking.

The duty will apply to all vaping products regardless of whether they contain nicotine.

Tobacco rates were also raised on Thursday, by £2.20 per 100 cigarettes or 50g of tobacco. HMRC said this maintains the financial incentive for smokers to switch to vaping.

Stocking up v cutting down

The BBC spoke to vapers in Reading who had mixed views on whether the new tax would encourage people to quit.

Mackenzie Bird, 19, has been a regular vaper for three years. She said she was "fine" with the duty and it wouldn't stop her from vaping.

"I don't know how many people it'll actually deter," she said.

"I'll probably just stock up."

However, Cara Lewis-Rimes and Dylan Killner said they might reconsider the habit in light of higher prices.

Cara said she thinks the changes will force vapers to cut down because of the cost of living.

Dylan said he might be inclined to quit altogether.

"I don't think it's doing me any favours... the health factor around it as well is not great."

Fighting illegal trade

HMRC is also launching a stamp for vaping products which are traceable throughout the supply chain.

All vapes sold in the UK must carry this stamp from April.

The new tax is also an effort to combat illicit trade, which is a growing problem on UK high streets. Last month, the prime minister announced new powers for councils that will address the decline of the high street, including the amount of vape shops.

Changes to planning law in England mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open.

Health Minister Karin Smyth said: "These measures are an important step in our ambition to tackle youth vaping by reducing the affordability of vaping products, which goes hand-in-hand with the work we are already doing to tackle the appeal and availability of vapes on our high streets."

James Murray, the Financial Secretary to the Treasury, said the government was "backing all those retailers who play by the rules".

But Jordan Apap, a sales assistant in Berkshire Vapers, said the new tax would "put a lot of strain on legitimate vape shops" that provide more specialist advice and services than convenience stores and phone shops that sell vapes.

"There is a real and genuine risk that we will cease to exist within a year or two," he said.

John Dunne, the director general of the UK Vaping Industry Association, said: "This is nothing short of a tax on public health."

He said vapes had helped "millions of adults cut down on or stop smoking".

"Protecting young people is essential. But that means stronger enforcement against illegal and rogue traders, not making legal vaping more expensive for adults trying to stay away from cigarettes."

Experts say vaping is much safer than smoking, but it is not risk free and the long-term effects are less clear.

A recent review of vaping studies found that it had an association with problems in children and young people including wheezing and coughing, poor oral and dental health, poor sleep, mental health problems and eye symptoms.

The NHS has said that children and non-smokers should never vape.

Additional reporting by Neranjana Elapatha

title: 美国CCC级公司债利差突破1000基点 创2023年地区性银行危机以来最高
content:
美国风险最高的公司债相较美国国债的利差升逾1000个基点，为2023年地区性银行危机以来首次。这样的风险溢价水平通常意味着违约、重组或损失的可能性较高。
评级为CCC、即垃圾债中最低等级的债券周三利差达到1007个基点，高于9月初的860个基点，为2023年3月以来最阔，当时发生地区性银行危机，投资者纷纷抛售高风险信用资产。
“主要驱动因素是经济表现不错，但并没有特别强劲，”嘉信理财固定收益研究与策略主管Collin Martin表示，“CCC级发行人是市场上风险最高的发行人，往往对利率变化最为敏感。”
自4月以来，CCC级债券利差持续上升，因为投资者开始预期美联储将转向收紧政策，以遏制通胀。全球收益率飙升推高债务偿付成本，也使再融资变得更加困难，从而给高杠杆借款人带来压力，而与此同时，大量债券和贷款正陆续到期。
策略师表示：
“风险最高的一批债券正在遭到抛售，这反映出市场担心，随着利率上升，多年来对困境债务反复重组、不断拖延问题的做法最终将付出代价，并引发新一轮违约潮。”

title: 内塔尼亚胡：飞行员试图让迪拜航空客机坠毁
content:
一架由迪拜航空执飞、从迪拜飞往特拉维夫的航班险些发生灾难。一名飞行员持刀刺伤同事，意图让飞机坠毁，客机一度急剧俯冲，最终紧急迫降沙特阿拉伯。
以色列总理内塔尼亚胡在一段视频中讲述了事发经过。他表示，一名乘客和一名机组人员成功闯入驾驶舱并制服袭击者。机上恰好还有另一组机组人员帮助设法稳定了飞机。
“他们避免了一场可怕的灾难，”他说。
据内塔尼亚胡在社交媒体上的一则帖子，被刺伤的飞行员名叫Smit Machchhar。
内塔尼亚胡写道：“我要向印度飞行员Smit Machchhar机长的非凡勇气致敬。尽管遭到刺伤并身受重伤，他仍奋起反抗，打开了驾驶舱舱门，让乘客和机组人员得以制服袭击者，避免了一场灾难性的空中事故。”
袭击者目前正接受沙特当局讯问。沙特塔布克机场早些时候表示，当地时间上午8：44收到FZ1073航班发出的求救信号，要求紧急降落，飞机约一小时后着陆。
Flightradar24数据显示，这架 波音 737在不到30秒内从巡航高度急坠逾1.4万英尺（4300米），速度接近音速。飞机随后重新爬升，并发出一般紧急求救信号，之后又发出所谓“非法干扰”呼叫，暗示可能发生劫机事件。
客机在短暂进入约旦领空后掉头180度，随后向西南方向飞往塔布克。
未经核实的照片显示飞机在沙特降落后垂直尾翼上的方向舵已经缺失。
Flydubai的737 MAX 8客机通常可搭载约174人。
内塔尼亚胡表示，航班上几乎所有乘客都是以色列人，参与制服袭击者的人“表现出了非凡的应变能力和勇气”。
“他们挽救了许多人的生命，”他说。
该航空公司在声明中表示，“这起事件背后的原因和动机尚不清楚，仍有待正式调查。”
一架前往接回这些乘客的航班已搭载乘客抵达特拉维夫。FlyDubai随后表示，在调查进行期间，将暂停往返以色列的航班。
随着各国建立国际航空安全协议和监管规定，近几十年来劫机事件已经越来越少。上世纪70年代发生多起劫机未遂和既遂事件后，以色列针对航班采取了全球最严格的安保措施之一。
Flydubai是阿联酋航空的姊妹航空公司，于2020年底开通特拉维夫和迪拜之间的每日航班。根据该公司网站，此后相关航班已增至每周70班。阿联酋也已成为以色列游客热门的度假目的地。

title: Conservatives pledge 'tough love' benefit rules for under-25s
content:
The Conservatives have said they would introduce new work requirements for under-25s claiming benefits in a "tough love" approach to youth joblessness.

Under the proposals, young people who are fit to work but have not worked for six months continuously would face new rules to qualify for payments, including daily attendance at a job centre or courses.

The party says the scheme would help tackle the almost one million people aged 16 to 24 in the UK who are not in education, employment or training, known as Neets.

But anti-poverty charity Trussell warned that people on Universal Credit can already not afford basic essentials, harming their ability to find and keep work.

Under the Tory proposals, those aged 18 to 24 who apply for Universal Credit but have not previously worked for a continuous period of six months or more, for at least 16 hours per week, would instead have to take part in a "Get to Work" scheme.

Rather than Universal Credit, they would receive a "Get to Work Allowance" paid at the same rate but requiring daily attendance at a job centre, on work experience or work readiness courses.

They would be assigned a manager and have to take part in job search workshops and interview preparation sessions.

The programme would last six months, or less if a participant secures a job - but those who are still unemployed after half a year on the scheme would have their benefit cut by 30%.

Young people on Universal Credit who have previously worked for six months, have health issues or care responsibilities would be exempt.

'Failings of a tick-box approach'

The party has also said it would look closer at whether parents' earnings and savings should be factored into welfare payments for their children.

However, it said young people without parental support, including those who are estranged, would continue to have a safety net.

Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said the measures were designed to "show some tough love" to reduce the number of Neets.

"Too many young people are leaving school and signing straight onto benefits - this is a waste of their potential and a disaster for our economy," the Tory MP said.

However, Helen Barnard, director of policy and research at anti-poverty charity Trussell, said the Tory proposals were "deeply concerning".

"We've got years of evidence of the failings of a tick-box approach. Meetings with over-stretched work coaches are already too short and often do little to actually move people into training or work," she said.

"We need more meaningful, good quality support, not simply more of the same."

Under current Universal Credit requirements, external, people have to sign a "claimant commitment" to prepare for and look for work or increase their earnings if they are already working - but the Tories claim their rules would be stricter.

The proposals were announced on Thursday ahead of the party's annual conference starting this weekend.

Neets have been high on the agenda for political parties ahead of the imminent publication of a major report by former minister Alan Milburn on how to tackle the one-in-eight young people in the UK who not in education, employment or training.

Labour Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said: "Kemi Badenoch's Tories held young people back and caused the welfare bill to spiral.

"To pretend she's suddenly on the side of young people is frankly insulting."

At Labour's conference earlier this week, Chancellor John Healey said cutting welfare spending was a priority and announced that every mayor in England would have access to a Local Apprenticeships Service from March 2027 to generate thousands more youth opportunities.

And on Thursday, the Department for Work and Pensions said every small and medium-sized business hiring a young apprentice would get £2,000 from the government under a new scheme backed by the Federation of Small Businesses.

title: 特朗普公布韩国对美能源项目投资计划 规模2000亿美元
content:
美国总统特朗普公布韩国对美国能源项目的投资计划，规模为2000亿美元，其中包括八座核电站、德克萨斯州一座发电设施以及阿拉斯加天然气出口项目。
“我们今天宣布的这一巨额投资计划，是确保关键能源供应链安全、保障美国能源主导地位，并使我们与韩国以及整个太平洋地区的伙伴关系比以往任何时候都更加牢固的重要一步，”特朗普周三在白宫活动上表示。能源行业高管也出席了这一活动。
这2000亿美元投资为去年美韩贸易协议下首批获得支持的项目，根据协议，韩国已承诺在美国投资3500亿美元。
这些计划公布之际，选民对生活成本以及特朗普管理美国经济的表现深感不满，使共和党面临在11月中期选举中失去国会控制权的风险。特朗普近日一直在宣传对一些共和党人选情吃紧州的投资，希望提振共和党的选情。
与特朗普一同出席活动的还有来自阿拉斯加州的共和党参议员Dan Sullivan，为了竞选连任，他正与前民主党众议员Mary Peltola展开激烈角逐。
Sullivan在椭圆形办公室表示，该项目将为阿拉斯加居民提供低成本能源，同时向美国在亚洲的盟友供应美国能源。这些项目可能需要数年才能投产，这意味着该州选民在投票前不太可能看到相关收益。
根据最新融资计划，韩国将把约1000亿美元投向美国多达八座核反应堆的建设。
美国商务部长卢特尼克表示，德克萨斯州另一座6.5吉瓦天然气发电厂的投资规模约为220亿美元。
有报道称，韩国计划向阿拉斯加州液化天然气项目提供540亿美元的资金支持。这一规划已久的项目旨在从该州的北坡输送天然气，一部分用于区域发电，其余部分液化并运往海外的亚洲买家。
虽然韩国的支持被视为有助于推动这一标志性项目取得进展，但知情人士称，韩国目前尚未对阿拉斯加液化天然气（LNG）项目做出全面承诺，资本投入预计还将取决于进一步的尽职调查和审查。
即便如此，此次宣布仍标志着阿拉斯加LNG项目向前迈出重要一步。这一计划已经酝酿数十年，但由于其庞大的投资成本和规模而面临障碍，其中包括在该州建设一条长达740英里管道的挑战。

title: ElevenLabs估值翻倍至220亿美元，完成3亿美元员工要约收购
content:
英国备受瞩目的AI音频生成公司ElevenLabs今日表示，其估值在不到一年内翻倍至220亿美元，同时完成了3亿美元的员工要约收购。
ElevenLabs首席执行官马蒂·斯塔尼谢夫斯基在X上宣布了要约收购完成，并发布了ElevenLabs的进展报告。该公司因利用AI将文本转换为听起来像真人朗读的语音而闻名。
现有投资者和员工在此次要约中出售了价值3亿英镑的股票，此次要约由Wellington和T Rowe Price领投。
220亿美元的估值较2月翻倍，当时该公司在D轮主要融资中筹集了5亿美元，估值达110亿美元。
ElevenLabs此前已进行过多次员工要约收购，旨在为员工提供流动性。
该公司表示，作为此次要约的一部分，EQT、 高盛 、GIC、OTPP、Sapphire Ventures和BDT & MSD首次投资ElevenLabs，与现有投资者Andreessen Horowitz、Lightspeed、Iconiq、D.E． Shaw、Evantic、Disruptive和Alkeon共同参与。
斯塔尼谢夫斯基重点介绍了ElevenLabs发布的两款新文本转语音模型，以及其AI平台。
斯塔尼谢夫斯基说：“AI应该以我们彼此互动的方式与人互动。做到这一点，将有助于确保AI在经济中广泛普及，让每个人都能塑造并受益于它，无论技术技能如何。
“我们已经看到企业和政府迅速采用富有表现力的语音代理，将其部署用于服务消费者和公民。随着我们成长，让我们的员工分享他们为客户和更广泛世界创造的部分价值，对我们来说很重要。”

title: 美防长：马斯克、帕尔默·拉基和纽特·金里奇将协助五角大楼推进战争计划
content:
美国国防部长赫格塞思周三表示，五角大楼正在邀请 特斯拉 和SpaceX首席执行官埃隆·马斯克、国防科技企业家兼Anduril联合创始人帕尔默·拉基以及前众议院议长纽特·金里奇，帮助确定美国未来战争可能需要的军事能力、技术和武器。
这项名为“子午线计划”的倡议将用120天时间展望未来数年乃至数十年，研究战争可能如何变化，以及美军需要哪些能力来保持技术优势。
“子午线计划，即战争的未来，不是要制定新战略或新政策，”赫格塞思说。相反，他说，其目的是“确定我们必须征服的领域，以及我们必须掌握的能力。”
赫格塞思说，这项工作将专注于“发现、开发和部署”未来美军可能需要的武器和系统，战场范围“从地下到月球之外”。他在弗吉尼亚州匡蒂科海军陆战队基地向初级军官和士兵领袖发表“部队状况”讲话时宣布了这一倡议。
赫格塞思说，五角大楼技术主管埃米尔·迈克尔将监督该项目，马斯克、拉基和金里奇担任联合负责人，更广泛的团队将来自政府、产业界、学术界和政策界。
这三位联合负责人都没有在美国军队服役过。马斯克曾表示，他十几岁时移居加拿大，部分原因是为了避免在南非服义务兵役。
这一角色使马斯克和拉基处于有利位置，可以帮助确定军方未来的技术需求，同时他们的公司正在竞争数十亿美元的国防部业务。
马斯克的SpaceX拥有大量五角大楼合同。5月，太空军授予该公司一份价值41.6亿美元的合同，建造旨在跟踪和瞄准空中威胁的卫星；就在几天前，太空军还授予SpaceX另一份价值22.9亿美元的军事卫星通信网络合同。
拉基的Anduril开发自主武器和其他军事技术。海军陆战队于2025年授予该公司一份价值高达6.42亿美元的合同，用于反无人机系统。
这一宣布是五角大楼更广泛推进自主战争的一部分，包括周三宣布的计划，即成立新的四星自主战争司令部，旨在在整个军队中扩大自主和机器人系统的规模。

title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal
content:
Another wave of landslides and heavy rain has killed about 30 people in Nepal, as the Himalayan nation reels from August's catastrophic flooding that left 1,400 dead and thousands more missing.

The national disaster management authority says more than 1,900 families have been affected since late last week with more than 240 homes damaged. Roads, buildings and bridges have been swept away.

Hundreds of trekkers on the Annapurna Circuit - crucial to Nepal's economy - have had to cut short their hikes to get to safety.

Many have been helicoptered out of the districts of Manang and Mustang, from a hiking circuit that usually takes up to three weeks to complete.

Communities in several parts of Nepal are mourning loved ones.

Speaking from a damp, blue tent in Battar, a town north-west of Kathmandu, Buti Tamang told BBC Nepali: "We used to live in a hut, but now there is nothing. We have lost so many of our relatives."

"Now it is raining and the tent leaks, so we've been facing a difficult situation. We have nowhere to go," said Ramesh Ghale, who also had to flee his home.

Several trekkers and their guides say their journeys back down the mountains have been treacherous, taking up to three or four days and requiring them to pass collapsed roads and swept-away bridges.

Jake Stacy, a 21-year-old from Suffolk, found himself stranded with his guide in Yak Kharka, upper Manang, due to heavy snowfall last week and decided not to continue to the Thorang La pass, the highest point of the circuit.

"We made our own paths on mountain slopes," he said, after returning to base camp in Pokhara on Tuesday night. "It was quite steep and we were clambering because there was river below… It was very muddy and very wet.

"Many trekkers were helicoptered out," he added.

Australian Andrew Graham and his guide Prem KC said they had to cross more than 15 landslides after they decided to return from Manang village. "A few of them were quite dangerous, the residual risks have grown now."

The two got stuck when they reached the village of Chame, which had been evacuated due to the risk of landslides, and had to spend a night in the jungle, Graham said.

A massive landslide has partially blocked a river which passes through Chame, causing a temporary lake that has inundated houses and a key bridge. Authorities have been trying to release the water for the past three days using excavators but have not been very successful, locals told the BBC.

Meanwhile, trekking guide Tse Ring Doma said she and her group had to cross 28 landslides. The mental stress was more difficult than the physical challenge, she said, given the fresh memory of last month's enormous disaster: "Even thunder would make us run and come out to see if anything was coming our way."

Her client, Norwegian Ellen Wahlström, said visitors were fortunate - they would only have to leave some of their items behind, while locals risked losing their houses and land. She added that authorities had been clearing many of the landslides "surprisingly fast".

While road damage in Manang has been serious, with several bridges swept away and communications down in some areas, no one had been killed in the trekking region, chief district officer Mukti Prasad Khanal said.

But four bodies have been recovered and 12 people remain missing after an avalanche near the base of Himlung Peak, close to the border with Tibet.

A representative of the local trekking authority, the Annapurna Conservation Area Project, said some 700 trekkers were still waiting in Pokhara to embark on the Annapurna Circuit.

"We have been holding back all these people who want to go to the Annapurna Circuit trek, although we are under pressure from the trekking industry to announce the route open," he said.

Indian visitors who often visit the ancient temple Muktinath on a Hindu pilgrimage had been asked to fly from Jomson to Pokhara instead of drive down, due to a cut-off road, he added.

Most of the old trekking trails on the Annapurna Circuit have been unused in recent years after the introduction of roads, except for small pockets of Manang and Mustang districts.

But now operators say many trekkers have been using these abandoned paths to return, as the main roads have been washed away in some sections of the circuit.

Additional reporting by BBC Nepali

title: The rare Bog Grass Moth found in nature reserve for first time
content:
A rare species of moth has been found in north Wales.

The Bog Grass Moth was found at Cors Geirch National Nature Reserve on the Llŷn Peninsula in Gwynedd, as conservationists were surveying the area's species.

Experts called it a "special surprise" to find the "incredibly sparse moth" in the habitat.

An exact population figure in the UK for the Bog Grass Moth is not known, but they have only been recorded in a small number of English counties, such as Dorset.

The fen, which is an area of low, flat, wet land, is monitored by Natur am Byth's Llŷn and Ynys Môn project, which aims to protect some of north Wales' most at risk species.

As experts from the conservation project gathered at Cors Geirch they set up moth traps and in one night 446 moths made up of 91 different species were collected, with 19 of these being Bog Grass Moths - the first time they had been recorded in this area.

Natural Resources Wales said the habitat allowed wet sedges to grow - which is the only food source for the Bog Grass Moth's larvae.

Sedges are one of the largest plant families in the world and are most common in wet habitats.

Other rare species recorded at the site included the Six Spotted Crane Fly and the Black Nightrunner Ground Beetle.

Steve Palin and Charles Aron, who are both lepidopterists and specialise in the study of moths, said the beauty of trapping moths was "you just never know what's going to turn up".

"It's a significant addition to our knowledge of the region's winged insects and demonstrates the value of targeted moth recordings in these specialist fen habitats, where there is clearly still much to discover," they said in a statement.

Clare Sampson, a project manager for RSPB Cymru, said the work of staff, contractors and volunteers had helped to open up the wetland that is "home to these rare invertebrate species".

She added: "While many fens suffered over the hot, dry summer, not only did we find healthy numbers of the Black Nightrunner Ground Beetle and Six Spotted Crane Fly at Cors Geirch this year, but we also discovered this wonderful and rare species of moth."

Sampson said about 80% of UK peatlands had been lost or damaged, meaning rare species that depend on specific habitats can "struggle to survive".

Healthy peat is the country's biggest carbon store but when damaged it releases planet-warming greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

Peat is formed over thousands of years from partially decayed plants in waterlogged conditions.

"These important fen sites can be managed and maintained so that future generations can continue to make new discoveries," she added.

title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn
content:
Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.

Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.

However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.

The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.

Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".

Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.

As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".

He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.

"It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'"

Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.

"Work experience needs to be mandatory. It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.

Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.

"There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said. "In other schools, students are told to go off and find their own work experience and that often relies on the network of Mum and Dad."

These recommendations are due to be published in the final instalment of his government-commissioned report into the issue, which is expected to be published in the autumn.

Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.

Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.

The government has said its vision, external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.

In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.

Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.

"In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.

"Just let them be little kids. I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids."

But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.

"I think it's a good idea," she says. "It's something that everyone has to do, so if you learn early, it's something they don't have to learn later on."

Teaching unions have responded positively to the idea of introducing career-based learning into schools at a younger age, but have warned about the burden this could place on primary schools in particular.

Paul Whiteman, general secretary of school leaders' union National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), warns of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools.

"Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.

Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".

"The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.

Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL), says having someone come into the classroom can really "enlighten [children's] motivation... and give them that sense of passion for all the opportunities beyond the classroom". Although he acknowledges that finding opportunities in rural areas could be more challenging.

title: 美元录得3月份以来最佳单月表现 美联储抗通胀立场推升利率预期
content:
随着美联储重新聚焦于遏制通胀，推动利率预期和美国国债收益率走高，美元录得3月份以来最佳单月表现。
美元指数9月上涨近2%，涨幅略超6月。周三，在美联储青睐的通胀指标 —— 个人消费支出（PCE）价格指数涨幅低于预期后，该指数一度下滑，但最终仍收高。美国长期国债收益率也升至数十年高点。
“低于预期的PCE数据正在给美元带来压力，并表明美联储10月加息基本已不在考虑之列，但12月加息仍有可能，”Monex Inc．外汇交易员Andrew Hazlett表示，“美元9月表现不错，我们预计这种走势将持续，因为美联储仍在继续努力恢复价格稳定。”
周三数据公布后，交易员调低了对美联储10月加息的预期，同时预计12月加息的概率达到100%。总体而言，市场预计未来12个月美联储将累计收紧货币政策约90个基点，这对美元构成支撑。美国经济数据稳健，加上通胀风险加剧，一直在推动美元和美国国债收益率走高。
Bank of America策略师Alex Cohen表示，市场关注焦点转向定于周五公布、更为重要的9月就业数据。
利差扩大以及美国经济增长强劲，正迫使一些美元空头重新审视自己的立场。 摩根士丹利 近期放弃了长期以来认为美元将在2026年下半年走弱的观点。不过，德意志银行仍坚持其看法，预计美元兑欧元到年底将下跌约3%。
9月，除日元外，所有十国集团（G10）货币兑美元均走弱。日本当局干预外汇市场的风险上升，以及市场对日本央行进一步加息的预期，均为日元提供支撑。
期权定价显示，交易员在各个期限上均看好美元。风险逆转目前接近6月份以来最看好美元的水平，该指标反映看涨与看跌需求的相对强弱。与此同时，一些指标开始显示美元涨势可能正在失去动能。一项衡量美元动能的指标周二升至70以上，表明美元可能处于超买状态；周三仍处于这一区域。
“我们认为美元开始显得有些涨过头了，”CIBC Capital Markets策略师Noah Buffam表示。

title: 10月1日外盘头条：特朗普称最后一批美军即将撤离伊拉克 谷歌推出Gemini 4 Argon 美光营收单季破540亿美元
content:
全球财经媒体昨夜今晨 共同关注的头条新闻主要有：
1、 特朗普：最后一批美军即将撤离伊拉克
2、 美联储监察长发现翻修工程存在失误，但无刑事移送依据
3、 谷歌推出最先进的AI模型Gemini 4 Argon
4 、 美光Q4营收单季破542亿美元 预判存储2027-2028持续供给紧缺
5、 Meta股价因AI势头创2022年以来最佳月度表现
6、 美联储首选通胀指标显示8月核心通胀为3.0%，远低于市场预期
特朗普：最后一批美军即将撤离伊拉克
特朗普宣布，最后一批美军即将撤离伊拉克。他表示，这段历程漫长，当初一系列糟糕的决策使美国陷入这场泥潭，而这段历史很快将会翻篇。
他称，这对美国而言是意义重大的一天，美军撤离时，伊拉克迎来了新任总理扎伊迪，特朗普自始至终都支持并全力背书扎伊迪，后者在原本不被看好的选举中以压倒性优势胜选。
特朗普称，“坚定决心行动”始于2003年小布什执政时期，2014年由奥巴马政府延续，之后拜登政府继续推进，这项行动将在2026年、由特朗普政府主导宣告结束。他认为这一天是美国的胜利、伊拉克的胜利，也是对ISIS的决定性胜利；ISIS在他首个总统任期内就遭到政府彻底摧毁，其他危险极端势力同样受到打击。
美联储监察长发现翻修工程存在失误，但无刑事移送依据
美联储监察长周三发布的一份报告认定，管理和监督失误导致央行总部翻修工程出现重大成本超支，但未发现刑事移送依据。
美联储监察长报告称：“在我们的评估过程中，我们从未发现合理依据认为发生了违反联邦刑法的行为，从而需要根据《监察长法》向美国司法部长移送。”
这家独立监督机构的调查结果可能化解针对前美联储主席鲍威尔的一条攻击线。特朗普总统和其他批评者曾指责鲍威尔对该项目管理不善，并就该项目误导国会。
谷歌推出最先进的AI模型Gemini 4 Argon
Alphabet周三推出了Gemini 4 Argon，这是其迄今最先进的人工智能模型，在编码、网络安全和复杂专业工作方面有重大改进。
该公司表示，该模型在真实世界软件工程方面创下新纪录，在网络安全方面并列第一，并在另一项衡量金融、法律及其他专业任务表现的基准测试中领先。
该公司称，Argon已在内部用于优化 谷歌 数据中心的内存，在没有购买额外硬件的情况下释放了数百TB内存。量子计算研究人员也已使用该模型。
美光Q4营收单季破542亿美元 预判存储2027-2028持续供给紧缺
美光 科技公布2026财年第四财季业绩，全部核心指标均超出业绩指引上限。
第四财季实现营收542.3亿美元，环比大涨31%，同比暴涨379%；非GAAP毛利率高达87.0%。
本财季非GAAP净利润383.98亿美元，摊薄每股收益33.42美元；经营现金流达到439.73亿美元，调整后自由现金流332.0亿美元，期末公司流动性储备高达754.8亿美元。
完整2026财年，美光总营收飙升至1331.88亿美元，同比增长256%；其中DRAM全年营收突破千亿美元大关，达1006.79亿美元。
Meta股价因AI势头创2022年以来最佳月度表现
Meta股价刚刚结束自2022年以来最佳月度表现，投资者欢呼这家社交媒体巨头近期在人工智能领域的势头。
该公司股价周三收于725.18美元，较8月底收盘价572.34美元上涨27%。自9月8日推出其Muse个人AI代理应用以来，华尔街一直对该公司业务持乐观态度，该应用大获成功，在 苹果 iOS下载量上超过了竞争对手OpenAI的ChatGPT。
Meta上一次月度表现更强劲是在2022年11月，即OpenAI推出ChatGPT的那个月。当时Meta在残酷的一年后正在反弹，并启动了效率提升行动。
美联储首选通胀指标显示8月核心通胀为3.0%，远低于市场预期
美国商务部周三公布数据：依据美联储主要通胀衡量指标，8 月消费者物价同比涨幅低于预期。
个人消费支出（PCE）物价指数经季节调整后当月环比上涨 0.3%，12 个月同比涨幅为3.4%。 道琼斯 调查的经济学家此前预期分别为环比 0.3%、同比 3.7%。
剔除食品与能源后的核心 PCE 物价指数环比上涨 0.2%，年度核心通胀达到 3.0%；市场此前预期分别为环比 0.3%、同比 3.3%。

title: Flydubai passenger describes putting attacker in chokehold after cockpit stabbing
content:
Passengers on a flight to Israel have recounted how they subdued a pilot after he stabbed the other pilot and appeared to be trying to disable the plane, while others described the "terrifying" moment they thought they would die.

Appearing in a bloodstained shirt after the ordeal, Yaniv Hayun told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu he realised something was wrong when the aircraft suddenly dropped.

The plane, en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv, plummeted 17,000ft (5,200m) in less than two minutes.

"Someone screamed... the light went out," Hayun said in a video posted by the prime minister on social media.

He and others tried to push open the cockpit door, but the pilot who had been stabbed was very close to it, so it was hard to open. Before he collapsed, the injured pilot managed to open the door.

When Hayun and another man entered the cockpit, he said he saw one pilot down and the attacker on the instruments, between the two seats, "trying to destroy the instruments in order to...disable the plane".

"I grabbed the attacker, put him in a chokehold, and pulled him - first and foremost - outside," Hayun said.

"We pulled him out; it was a matter of seconds. I called out to the Israeli guys with us on the plane - I called them, and two other guys came over to me... we pinned [the attacker] down to keep him secure."

Hayun said he then jumped back into the cockpit and "started pulling the controls".

When asked by Netanyahu whether he knew what he was doing, the passenger answered: "I watch Air Crash Investigation, Mr Prime Minister."

Hayun said the plane then started to level out. By then, two on-duty pilots who had been in the passenger cabin were at the front of the plane, and one told Hayun he was taking control from there.

Netanyahu praised Hayun, calling him a "great hero" and a "lion".

Another passenger, Zvika Meness, told Israeli public broadcaster Kan he helped overpower the attacker, and the passenger and two others "tied him up with his own zip ties and with the multimedia headphones".

"Another pilot who was sitting in the passenger cabin went in to replace the additional pilot, and they essentially landed the plane," he added.

Follow live updates

The Flydubai flight eventually landed at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, and the passengers were later taken to Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion airport on a repatriation aircraft.

They were greeted by crowds of onlookers playing music, singing, dancing and waving Israeli flags.

"Thank God I'm alive," passenger Haim Lazarovich told journalists, adding that "the most terrifying moment in this flight was when the pilot loses control".

Oran Choen, an 18-year-old passenger, described the incident as "a very tough moment".

"Maybe it was five minutes, but it feels like hell - I heard my brother behind me scream that we was going to die," he added.

A paramedic from Israel's ambulance service later told the BBC that a number of people were "very emotional and crying as they came off the plane".

The stabbed pilot, Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, was taken to hospital but is in stable condition, according to the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia.

Netanyahu praised Machchhar as a "true hero" of "extraordinary bravery".

The attacker was arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has called it an "attempted jihadist terror attack". No official motive for the incident or further information has been given.

US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu following the incident, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind the attack.

title: 全球债市单季表现创2024年以来最差 投资者担忧通胀
content:
全球政府债券正以2024年以来最差的季度表现收官，100美元的油价让全球经济再度面临顽固通胀的威胁。
彭博一项政府债券指数迈向2024年四季度以来最大单季跌幅；当时，唐纳德·特朗普赢得第二个美国总统任期，投资者开始为更具扩张性的财政政策做准备。
美国国债在最近这轮抛售中遭到重创，30年期收益率升至5.64%，创2002年以来最高。较短期限债券同期亦遭抛售。
中东冲突持续、人工智能支出蓬勃增长以及美国经济强劲，都在向投资者发出信号：通胀问题可能比他们此前预期的更加严重。澳大利亚、欧元区、日本、挪威和美国的央行过去三个月均加息以应对。
“第三季度不只是打消了对利率‘更低更久’的憧憬，简直像是给这些希望浇上稀缺的柴油，再一把火烧掉，”荷兰合作银行全球策略师Michael Every表示，并称，现在最大的问题在于，还会加几次息。
美国方面，美联储青睐的通胀指标低于预期后，交易员周三削减了对美联储10月再次加息的押注。交易员仍预计未来一年至少还会加息三次。
全球压力
在其他主要债券市场中，法国抛售最严重。随着明年总统选举临近，投资者情绪紧张；距离投票仅剩七个月，反对党一直不愿对总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙即将卸任的政府作出让步。
法国10年期国债收益率单季上升1.15个百分点，至4.8%，创至少自1999年欧元诞生以来最差季度表现。
法国国债周三表现落后，此前最新通胀数据显示，该国9月物价涨幅加快至两年多来最快，给欧洲央行决策者带来更大压力。

title: 10月1日热门中概股多数上涨 京东贝壳理想涨超1% BOSS直聘涨超4%

title: 搬出司法部和起诉威吓 特朗普逼鲍威尔从美联储理事会辞职

title: 原油：油价维持在100美元附近 中东石油供应据估接近战前水平
content:
油价在每桶100美元附近波动，华尔街分析师和交易员表示，经霍尔木兹海峡的石油流量正恢复至接近战前的水平，为全球原油市场带来急需的供应。
12月交割的布伦特原油期货收于每桶98美元上方，周三到期的11月合约突破103美元。
尽管原油价格远低于伊朗冲突期间的峰值，但仍高于夏季平均水平。
摩根大通 和 高盛 这两家华尔街大行均表示，中东原油输出规模接近战前水平。
此前沙特阿拉伯提高了经一条关键输油管道运往红海港口的原油输送量。
分析公司Kpler的数据也支持这一判断，交易员和船东私下表示，他们看到大量原油经霍尔木兹海峡进入市场。
不过， 美国银行 全球研究大宗商品研究主管Francisco Blanch表示，尚不清楚经霍尔木兹海峡增加的石油运输量能否持续。
他接受采访时表示：“这是否与正在进行的美伊谈判有关？或者，美国已从伊朗手中夺取了对海峡的控制权？如果是后一种情况，我认为我们可以预计石油运输量将继续维持在较高水平”。
交投最为活跃的布伦特12月合约上涨1.9%，结算价报每桶98.03美元。
周三到期的11月合约上涨0.9%，结算价报每桶103.53美元。
11月交割的WTI上涨1.2%，结算价报每桶90.42美元。

title: US film-maker loses 'Downton Shabby' High Court case
content:
An American man has lost his legal bid to take ownership of a historic mansion for £1.

Hopwood DePree, who claims ancestral links to the Grade II-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton, Rochdale, said he was "incredibly disappointed" after a judge at the High Court in Manchester ruled against him.

DePree, an actor and filmmaker, argued a 2017 agreement with Rochdale Council gave him the option to buy the manor house after securing planning permission to restore and redevelop it.

However, Judge David Hodge KC found the conditions required for ownership of the property to transfer had not been met.

Despite its current state, Hopwood Hall was described as being in the top 10% of most important listed buildings in England, the court heard.

DePree's plans included a wedding venue, hotel accommodation and visitor attractions aimed at bringing the hall back to life.

However, Rochdale Council decided in 2022 not to transfer ownership of the hall to DePree and later locked him and a group of volunteers out of the site.

The court heard the legal costs were about £150,000, with the council expected to seek an order requiring DePree to pay them.

A Rochdale Council spokesperson said the council was pleased with the judgment.

"It's a shame that we had to endure a costly court battle to get to this point, as the time and money invested in this process could have been better spent on the hall itself," they said.

The spokesperson said more than £1.6m had been spent on the hall by the council and Historic England since 2017, and that investment in vital repairs would continue while its long-term future was "considered in due course".

They added that, once restored and refurbished, the building would be "used for the benefit of the wider community of Middleton who rightly cherish it as an important part of Middleton's rich and varied heritage".

DePree published a book about his campaign to restore the hall in 2022, titled Downton Shabby.

Speaking after the ruling, he said he was "incredibly disappointed" and described it as "a sad day".

He said he was discussing next steps with his legal team, adding: "We are not giving up. Hopwood Hall must be saved."

"I am getting messages from around the world from people offering money and support," he added.

title: 美光Q4营收单季破542亿美元 预判存储2027-2028持续供给紧缺
content:
美光 科技公布2026财年第四财季业绩，全部核心指标均超出业绩指引上限。
第四财季实现营收542.3亿美元，环比大涨31%，同比暴涨379%；非GAAP毛利率高达87.0%。
本财季非GAAP净利润383.98亿美元，摊薄每股收益33.42美元；经营现金流达到439.73亿美元，调整后自由现金流332.0亿美元，期末公司流动性储备高达754.8亿美元。
完整2026财年，美光总营收飙升至1331.88亿美元，同比增长256%；其中DRAM全年营收突破千亿美元大关，达1006.79亿美元。
AI驱动四大业务全线走高，数据中心SSD单季营收近百亿美元
AI算力需求拉动各事业部营收集体创新高：
1． 核心数据中心业务（CDBU）营收180.02亿美元，环比暴增56%，毛利率90%。数据中心SSD单季营收接近100亿美元，较去年同期增长超10倍，公司预计2026年将连续第五年拿下数据中心SSD市占率历史新高。
2． 云内存业务CMBU（以HBM为主）营收162.83亿美元，毛利率83%。HBM出货增速跑赢公司整体营收；美光已锁定2027年绝大多数HBM比特供应量，产品售价同比大幅上行，HBM与普通DRAM的毛利率差距持续收窄。公司正与英伟达联合开发定制NVHBM（HBM4E），将用于下一代GPU与NVLink Fusion平台。
3． 移动与客户端业务MCBU营收131.14亿美元，毛利率90%；新一代1γ DRAM产品已占到该板块近半数营收。
4． 汽车与嵌入式AEBU营收68.24亿美元，环比增长47%。管理层看好物理AI赛道，L4以上自动驾驶内存需求超200GB，人形机器人存储需求对标高阶自动驾驶，多家客户已经开始采样下一代存储产品。
分产品维度：DRAM本季营收397.71亿美元，ASP环比高双位数上涨；NAND营收141.02亿美元，ASP环比大涨30%，比特出货环比增长10%。
手握320亿客户长单！26份战略锁量协议，部分合约延至2031年
美光披露战略客户协议（SCA）进展：目前已经签署26份多年期“照付不议”长单，预计到2030年，长单收入占公司总营收比重将超过35%。
客户给出的财务承诺总额达到320亿美元，绝大部分为现金定金。四分之三的长单设置价格地板与天花板，剩余部分跟随市场动态议价；已有部分合约将期限拓展至2031年，新签订长单均参考当前市场高价执行。长单稳定了美光长期供给规划，同时给下游客户锁定产能。
下财季指引：Q1 FY2027营收看615亿美元，毛利率为本财年谷底
美光给出2027财年第一财季业绩展望（非‑GAAP）：
- 营收：615亿美元，上下浮动15亿美元
- 毛利率约86.25%，管理层提示Q1将是FY2027全年毛利率低点，后续季度毛利率再度回升
- 摊薄每股收益38.15美元，浮动±1美元，有效税率约15.5%
FY2027整体判断：公司预计全年营收逐季环比增长，再创年度业绩新高；全年运营费用预计增加约25亿美元，主要投向AI相关研发以及员工绩效激励。受Q4计提高额员工奖金存货结转影响，成本压力将集中体现在2027财年Q1。分红方面，每股0.15美元将于10月29日发放。
行业重磅判断：存储供需缺口持续，尚未看到市场重回平衡时间点
美光管理层给出存储周期核心判断：2027‑2028年DRAM、NAND行业将持续供给紧张，目前看不到供需回归平衡的明确时间窗口。
即便全行业推进洁净室扩产，叠加AI带来持续超预期的增量需求，结构性缺口依旧存在。
- DRAM：2026行业比特出货中双位数增长；2027‑2028降至低双位数增长，供给持续受限。
- NAND：2026行业比特出货低20%+增长；2027‑2028维持中20%+增速，供不应求。
- HBM比特出货增速将持续显著高于普通DRAM至2028年。
全球多点砸钱扩产，资本开支上调，多家新工厂2027‑2030陆续落地
面对紧缺格局，美光决定上调2027财年资本开支计划，新增资金主要投向洁净室土建，保障2028年末之后新增产能释放。
全球产能布局节点：
- 美国：ID1工厂预计2027年年中产出晶圆；ID2工厂2028年末；纽约新工厂要到2030年才能投产。
- 新加坡：HBM先进封装厂房进度超前，2027年初投产；全新NAND厂房2028下半年投产。
- 日本DRAM新工厂破土，2028年末初步产出。
公司提示：新建晶圆厂从产出晶圆到产能爬坡贡献营收，需要经历多个季度。
管理层人事更新
财报同步公布高管任命：
1． 马尼什·巴蒂亚（Manish Bhatia）出任总裁兼首席运营官COO，全盘负责业务单元、全球运营，承担公司整体盈亏责任。
2． 斯科特·德布尔（Scott DeBoer）博士出任总裁兼首席技术与产品官，掌管全公司技术路线图、研发以及美光研究院。

title: Meta股价因AI势头创2022年以来最佳月度表现
content:
Meta股价刚刚结束自2022年以来最佳月度表现，投资者欢呼这家社交媒体巨头近期在人工智能领域的势头。
该公司股价周三收于725.18美元，较8月底收盘价572.34美元上涨27%。自9月8日推出其Muse个人AI代理应用以来，华尔街一直对该公司业务持乐观态度，该应用大获成功，在 苹果 iOS下载量上超过了竞争对手OpenAI的ChatGPT。
Meta上一次月度表现更强劲是在2022年11月，即OpenAI推出ChatGPT的那个月。当时Meta在残酷的一年后正在反弹，并启动了效率提升行动。
Meta还在9月举行了年度Connect开发者大会，当时扎克伯格将Muse描述为其产品和业务战略的“核心”，同时发布了新的硬件产品，如Muse Charm AI吊坠。
随着该公司看好新兴AI代理市场的潜在巨大商机，OpenAI等竞争对手也在做同样的事，后者周二推出了其Dots代理工具。与此同时，Meta本周还聘请了MongoDB首席执行官CJ Desai领导其名为Meta Enterprise Platform的新业务部门，同时推出了面向小企业的Muse代理技术。
“包括云容量在内的企业AI解决方案市场，预计到2028年将超过1万亿美元，我们认为Meta的消费者数据和通信应用可能为Meta向面向消费者的公司销售AI企业产品带来优势，” 美国银行 全球研究分析师在周一的一份报告中写道。“我们预计Meta的模型API将在领先的超大规模云平台上分发。”
9月也是Meta有记录以来第五好的月份。该股表现优于所有大型科技股同行，并大幅跑赢 纳斯达克 指数，后者在此期间上涨近2%。
